assumptions.statement: Students would rather run planning, learning, campus, money and career in one app than in a few specialised ones.
assumptions.kill: Most participants name a separate tool they would keep for the same job and cannot say what consolidation would give them.

assumptions.statement: Institutions will adopt one platform that replaces several existing systems, not only coexist beside them.

origin.where: audit PDF pp.19-22, four operating modes

assumptions.kill: No interviewed institution describes a replacement scenario inside its own planning horizon.

assumptions.statement: Institutions will grant SIS, LMS and identity access to a student-originated vendor.
assumptions.kill: Reviews describe read access for third-party tools as blocked or as requiring a contract the vendor cannot meet.

assumptions.statement: Students adopt a planner on their own, without an institutional mandate, and keep using it.

origin.where: founder thesis; VALIDATED.md names zero users

assumptions.kill: Fewer than half of the pilot panel still open it after the 34-day band and none can name something they would miss.

assumptions.statement: Students keep deadlines in several unconnected places, and the fragmentation causes missed or late work.

origin.where: audit PDF p.2 prompt; PILOT.md question 1

assumptions.kill: Participants' last near-miss traces to causes other than fragmentation (forgetting, workload, unclear policy).

assumptions.statement: Students understand the single dominant next action on Today, can say why it is shown, and act on or deliberately defer it.
assumptions.kill: Fewer than four of five participants in a segment state the action and its reason unaided.

assumptions.statement: Manual course entry is an acceptable first-class route when import is unavailable.
assumptions.kill: Participants abandon at manual entry or add placeholder data instead of real courses.

assumptions.statement: Local-first with optional account sync is enough to satisfy students' privacy expectations.
assumptions.kill: Participants decline to sign in or use real data because of data location, despite the explanation.

assumptions.statement: Syllabus import saves meaningful time over manual entry and is accurate enough to trust.

origin.where: PILOT.md question 4, gate 98% exact and 100% cited

assumptions.kill: Corrections after import take as long as manual entry, or the exactness gate is missed on real syllabi.

assumptions.statement: Students use AI help for coursework and want answers tied to the sources they were given.
assumptions.kill: Participants do not use AI help for coursework or ignore sources when shown.

assumptions.statement: Students can read provenance labels (official, connected, user-created, AI-generated, estimated) correctly.
assumptions.kill: Participants misread official versus AI-generated in more than one task in a segment.

assumptions.statement: Individual students will pay $7.99 a month or $59 a year for Plus.

origin.where: prices live per BILLING-LIVE-ACCEPTANCE-2026-10-03; no willingness observation

assumptions.kill: Participants at the money rung decline at that price and cannot name a price they would pay.

assumptions.statement: The free tier with a shared AI allowance of 60 generations a month is generous enough to build habit.
assumptions.kill: Participants reach the cap in the first fortnight or abandon when they approach it.

assumptions.statement: Priority student flows need to work offline or on weak connections.
assumptions.kill: Participants report essentially always-on connectivity and no lost work from outages.

assumptions.statement: Students want documents, sheets and decks inside the planner, with real-time collaboration, instead of their current Office or Google tools.
assumptions.kill: Participants keep their current tools for these jobs and do not want a second copy.

assumptions.statement: Students will share selected items with a guardian, and want to.
assumptions.kill: Students refuse or want sharing limited to nothing the guardian currently lacks.

assumptions.statement: Students use dining, housing, maps and directory features inside a planner rather than their campus apps.
assumptions.kill: Participants name existing campus apps they prefer and do not look for these features in a planner.

assumptions.statement: The first-win journey can be completed unaided by users of screen readers, magnification, keyboard-only and reading-support settings.

origin.where: EVIDENCE-REGISTER.md: automated and structural checks only

assumptions.kill: Any assistive-technology participant cannot complete a first-win task unaided.

assumptions.statement: The reading, display and input settings the product offers meet the needs of students who rely on them.
assumptions.kill: Participants who need a setting report that it does not hold across screens.

assumptions.statement: Faculty will publish materials and policy into a source pack and keep it current.
assumptions.kill: Faculty describe course materials as changing faster than any maintained pack could track.

assumptions.statement: Faculty accept students receiving AI answers grounded in their own course materials.
assumptions.kill: Faculty reject the use outright or set conditions the product cannot meet.

assumptions.statement: A student-approved agenda improves an advising meeting.
assumptions.kill: Advisors do not use the agenda, or find it adds preparation time with no change in what happens.

assumptions.statement: Advisors accept student-supplied context as input but never as the record.
assumptions.kill: Advisors rely on student-supplied context as if official, or refuse to look at it at all.

assumptions.statement: Registrars permit read-only enrollment and schedule feeds to a third-party student tool.
assumptions.kill: Policy or practice forbids third-party feeds regardless of student consent.

assumptions.statement: The correction loop (student flags, office fixes, source updates) matches how corrections actually flow.
assumptions.kill: Observed corrections run through channels the loop does not include.

assumptions.statement: Bill and aid visibility can be offered without account-level access.
assumptions.kill: The questions students bring need account views that no third party may hold.

assumptions.statement: Institutions will accept a payments role for Semester, directly or through a processor.
assumptions.kill: Offices treat any payment role as out of scope for a vendor of this kind.

assumptions.statement: Routing students to the right office reduces misroutes and repeat contacts.
assumptions.kill: Offices cannot say where students are misrouted today, or the routes in use are already correct.

assumptions.statement: Offices can publish the capacity, wait time and owner a handoff requires.
assumptions.kill: Offices cannot state capacity or wait for the handoff in question.

assumptions.statement: A manual, read-only first pilot clears an institution's security and privacy review without bespoke work.
assumptions.kill: Reviews require items the pilot design cannot supply (assurance reports, integrations, contracts).

assumptions.statement: Procurement is decided on the evidence-room items the audit lists (VPAT, DPA, penetration test, questionnaire library) and not on others.
assumptions.kill: Reviews turn on other items or on a champion's backing instead.

assumptions.statement: Institutions will use privacy-floored aggregate reporting (cells under ten suppressed) as useful.
assumptions.kill: Institutional research staff say the floor makes reports too sparse to use.

assumptions.statement: Guardians want progress visibility and accept granular, student-controlled, expiring access in place of full visibility.
assumptions.kill: Guardians reject student-controlled limits, or sharing causes disagreement the design cannot resolve.

assumptions.statement: Guardians will pay for a family tier.
assumptions.kill: Guardians would not pay, or only for outcomes the product cannot promise.

assumptions.statement: Employers will pay for seats or campaigns on a campus-bound talent network.
assumptions.kill: Employers recruit through channels they would not change and name no budget line.

assumptions.statement: Verified-achievement credentials change employers' hiring decisions.
assumptions.kill: Employers cannot name a credential that has changed a decision.

assumptions.statement: Alumni keep using a student-era identity after graduating, and institutions sponsor an alumni module.
assumptions.kill: Alumni drop student tools on leaving and no institution budgets for the module.

assumptions.statement: Providers will list on a marketplace with commissions, disputes and payouts.
assumptions.kill: Providers already reach students by other means and decline platform terms.

assumptions.statement: Campus vendors will integrate with a student-side platform on workable terms.
assumptions.kill: Vendors' terms forbid it or price it beyond reach.

assumptions.statement: Students accept an assistant that proposes actions and defers consequential ones to their confirmation, and do not find that a burden.
assumptions.kill: Participants find confirmation intrusive or approve without reading.

assumptions.statement: Students want one Today surface for their whole educational life, not only academic tasks.
assumptions.kill: Participants want Today limited to coursework and deadlines.

assumptions.statement: Thirty-day return follows from completing the first win.

origin.where: VALIDATED.md names this the missing number

assumptions.kill: First-win completers return at no higher a rate than non-completers across the panel.

assumptions.statement: Using Semester reduces missed or late deadlines.

origin.where: audit PDF p.14 job to be done

assumptions.kill: Panel reports of slipped work do not fall relative to baseline and later cohorts.

assumptions.statement: Students rely on published-information degree and registration planning while the official audit stays authoritative, and understand the difference.
assumptions.kill: Participants treat the plan as official, or ignore it.

assumptions.statement: Students return to generated study aids repeatedly across a term.
assumptions.kill: Study aids are used once and not again.

assumptions.statement: Students want messaging, groups and community inside the planner rather than in their existing channels.
assumptions.kill: Participants say their existing channels cover it and a new one is a cost.

assumptions.statement: Advisors will use a Semester caseload view in place of or beside their current advising system.
assumptions.kill: Advisors keep all working state in their existing system and treat additions as duplicate entry.

assumptions.statement: A school can configure roles, policies and integrations itself without bespoke work.
assumptions.kill: Observed configuration needs vendor staff for tasks the design assigns to the school.

assumptions.statement: Students can find export and deletion, and correctly say what will and will not happen when they use them.
assumptions.kill: Participants cannot find the controls or misstate what deletion removes.

assumptions.statement: Students already keep a calendar for classes and commitments, and want deadlines to appear in it rather than in a separate view.

origin.where: audit PDF p.8 calendar and time row

assumptions.kill: Participants do not use a calendar for school, or reject deadlines appearing in it.
